focalPoint.why: largest, whitest, highest-contrast shape; black outline against the mid-tone scene

zoneSplit.screenshotOnly: x 1.6-70, y 3-72 (about 46% of the frame): HUD, equipment column, whole battle
zoneSplit.mixed: x 70-100, y 33-90 (cat over scene) and x 0-23, y 64-100 (bush over equipment)
zoneSplit.marketingDominant: y 72-100 full width (headline, pill, cut-outs, grass)

areaBudget.note: percent of image pixels, silhouette-based estimates; bbox union of the marketing layer is ~48%

composition.balance: Heavy white mass on the right (cat, 29% wide, 57% tall) counter-weighted by the text block anchored far-left (headline from x 1.6) - a bottom-left to right diagonal. The bright slash FX at (40, 48) keeps the scene's centre alive between them.
composition.angles: Everything is 0 deg (UI, type, cut-outs) except the second card outline, tilted ~1.5 deg clockwise - a 'sticker' wobble that says 'this is a framed screenshot', not a screen.
layerSeparation: Card metaphor: 6 px white stroke + flat blue margin + a second tilted outline turn the screenshot into an object on a page.
Scale jump: the cut-outs are 2-4x the size of the in-game units and drawn with thick black outlines, while the in-game sprites have thin outlines.
White halo (M4.1) between the cat and the scene.
Depth of field: only the marketing foreground (M7) is blurred; the screenshot is uniformly crisp.
Type: the headline's double outline (white + dark blue) is the same device the in-game damage numbers use, so the text reads as part of the game's voice while sitting in a marketing position.

measured.method: PIL/numpy colour-threshold masks in tight regions, connected components (scipy.ndimage) for the cat, least-squares line fits for the tilted outline; +/-1% expected
